title: Senior AI Platform Engineer
full_description: Join ABC Fitness and become part of a culture that’s as ambitious as it is authentic. Let’s transform the future of fitness—together! Our Values Best Life We believe great work begins with great people. That’s why our culture is built on respect, trust, and belonging. We create an inclusive environment where every team member can bring their authentic self to work—because diverse perspectives drive innovation and meaningful impact. Growth Mindset We are doers, thinkers, and dreamers. At ABC Fitness, your growth is our investment. Through continuous learning, mentorship, and professional development opportunities, we empower you to reach new heights—personally and professionally. One Team From day one, you’ll be part of a team that collaborates, celebrates, and cares. We move fast, support one another, and have fun along the way. Because when you thrive, we all thrive. Location: Hyderabad, Telangana, India This role requires working from our local Hyderabad office 2-3x a week . ABC Fitness is building an intelligent platform for the fitness industry, with AI embedded into the products, workflows, and decision points our customers rely on every day. The AI Platform team builds the foundational capabilities that enable engineering and product teams to safely and reliably develop, deploy, and operate AI-powered experiences. This includes the LLM gateway, developer tooling, coding agents, inline guardrails, evaluation frameworks, retrieval capabilities, and the platform services that support production AI use cases. Our customers are the engineers building these systems and the product teams delivering AI features to users. As an AI Platform Engineer, you will own platform deliverables end to end. You’ll design, build, launch, instrument, and operate capabilities against clearly defined SLOs. You’ll make adoption easy through clean interfaces, thoughtful migration paths, and documentation that enables teams to use the platform independently. You’ll also help establish a clear architectural boundary: mechanism belongs in the request path, while policy sits outside it. The gateway executes routing and other policies but does not define them. This is a highly hands-on role for someone who combines strong platform engineering fundamentals with practical experience building and operating reliable AI systems. This is not a model-training or research role. We value demonstrated evidence of ownership and impact over a specific number of years or a previous job title containing “AI.” What You'll Do Own an AI platform deliverable from problem definition through production launch, adoption, and ongoing operation. Design, build, and operate platform capabilities such as LLM gateways, retrieval systems, agents, developer tooling, evaluation frameworks, and inline guardrails. Define success criteria and measurable outcomes before building, then use production data and baseline metrics to guide future improvements. Design systems with clear SLOs, strong observability, predictable failure handling, and reliable operational processes. Develop and maintain clean interfaces, migration paths, documentation, and paved paths that make platform adoption simple for engineering teams. Build retrieval and agent systems with a clear separation between retrieval quality and answer quality, supported by meaningful evaluation strategies. Design for secure and controlled AI execution, including least-privilege access, multi-tenant isolation, permissioning, auditability, and operational boundaries. Apply strong distributed systems principles, including consistency, idempotency, concurrency, resilience, rollout strategies, and failure-mode analysis. Use coding agents and other AI development tools effectively while validating their output through testing, review, and sound engineering judgment. Carry operational ownership for the systems you build, including participation in an on-call rotation, incident response, and post-incident improvement. Partner closely with Engineering, Product, Security, Infrastructure, SRE, and Developer Experience teams to ensure platform capabilities are practical, scalable, and widely adopted. Establish and communicate reusable technical patterns, standards, and reference implementations for building production-ready AI systems. WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Demonstrated experience building or operating production retrieval systems, agent platforms, AI tooling, or other AI-enabled capabilities that real users depend on. Strong software engineering experience designing and operating distributed systems within an existing architecture. The ability to identify and clearly reason about consistency, idempotency, concurrency, failure modes, multi-tenant isolation, security, and rollout risks. Practical understanding of AI system quality, including retrieval evaluation, answer quality, release gates, agent reliability, and cost per request. Experience designing systems with clear success criteria, measurable baselines, observability, and operational targets such as SLOs. Strong understanding of secure AI execution patterns, including least-privilege access, permissioning, auditability, and policy enforcement. Experience taking a platform or product capability from problem definition to production and remaining accountable for its reliability, adoption, and continued improvement. Ability to work effectively with coding agents and AI development tools, while independently verifying generated code and recommendations. A strong production mindset, including experience with incident response, on-call operations, monitoring, debugging, and post-incident learning. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to make complex technical concepts accessible to engineering and product stakeholders. A customer-focused mindset: you understand that a platform capability that teams do not adopt is not a successful outcome. A One Team orientation and a willingness to create reusable capabilities that enable other engineering teams to move faster and more safely. AND IT'S GREAT TO HAVE Experience with LLM gateways, agent frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluation systems, or AI developer platforms. Experience with FinOps, cost optimization, or usage-based measurement for AI systems. Experience in application security, policy enforcement, identity, access management, or secure platform design. Experience with search quality, ranking, experimentation, or relevance evaluation. Experience with OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, AI observability, or production telemetry. Experience building multi-tenant infrastructure or internal developer platforms. Experience with developer advocacy, technical enablement, SDKs, documentation, or helping teams adopt new engineering capabilities. Familiarity with routing systems, API gateways, service orchestration, workflow engines, or platform control planes. What Success Looks Like You own at least one platform deliverable end to end, with clear success criteria, measurable baseline metrics, and a stated SLO. Engineering teams can adopt the capability through a clean interface, clear documentation, and a practical migration path without requiring ongoing support from you. AI platform releases are evaluated using meaningful quality, reliability, latency, adoption, and cost metrics. Retrieval quality, answer quality, agent behavior, and production reliability are measured separately and improved deliberately. Agents and AI systems operate with least-privilege access, appropriate isolation, strong observability, and clear operational controls. The platform remains reliable in production, with effective incident response, clear ownership, and continuous improvement after failures. Engineers and product teams use the platform to deliver AI-powered capabilities faster, more safely, and with greater confidence. Within your first 90 days, you own a platform deliverable and understand your team’s baseline metrics—not only its target outcomes. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU: Purpose led company with a Values focused culture – Best Life, One Team, Growth Mindset Time Off – competitive PTO plans with 15 Earned accrued leave, 12 days Sick leave, and 12 days Casual leave per year 11 Holidays plus 4 Days of Disconnect – once a quarter, we take a collective breather and enjoy a day off together around the globe. #oneteam Group Mediclaim insurance coverage of INR 500,000 for employee + spouse, 2 kids, and parents or parent-in-laws, and including EAP counseling Life Insurance and Personal Accident Insurance Best Life Perk – we are committed to meeting you wherever you are in your fitness journey with a quarterly reimbursement Premium Calm App – enjoy tranquility with a Calm App subscription for you and up to 4 dependents over the age of 16 Support for working women with financial aid towards crèche facility, ensuring a safe and nurturing environment for their little ones while they focus on their careers At ABC Fitness, we don’t just build technology—we build communities and transform lives. Your work matters here, your growth is supported, and your voice is heard. We welcome diverse talent and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every requirement. title: Staff Engineer
full_description: This role is responsible for two things that are more connected than they first appear: (1) making production deployments safe enough that rollback is the default response to a problem, and (2) making configuration changes safe, audited, and AI-supervised so that bad configuration is caught before it reaches production. Both are fundamentally release-safety problems. GreyOrange operates a platform that multiple enterprise customers (DHL, XPO, Continental, others) run in production warehouses. A bad deployment or a bad configuration change is a customer-visible incident. The infrastructure you build is what stands between a code change and a customer outage. The company's ability to keep all customers on the same major platform version — rather than maintaining separate branches per customer — depends entirely on whether rollback is fast, trustworthy, and routine. After establishing the deployment and configuration management foundations, you expand into data and messaging engineering — specifically Kafka schema contracts and the Redis claim-check pattern for payload management. The overlap between distributed delivery systems (Kubernetes + Kafka both require schema and contract thinking) makes this a natural progression. What You Will Do First Six Months - Deployment Safety & Configuration Take ownership of the deploy and release engineering domain. Maintain the deployment and configuration systems as production services — they are part of the platform team's on-call rotation. Contribute to cross-team architecture reviews with a deployment safety and release-engineering lens. Write and maintain design documents and runbooks for everything you build. full_description: Data Scientist, Response EvaluationJob DescriptionAbout Uplevyl Uplevyl builds AI-powered knowledge and community infrastructure for organizations serving women. Our products include UpGenie (our domain-specific AI assistant), WeHub (our community platform) and UpSocial (a social platform for women). We work with mission-driven partners to turn complex, high-stakes information into clear, trustworthy guidance, and to build systems that create lasting impact. We hold a simple conviction: in high-stakes domains like rights, law and financial security, a generic AI is not enough. The answers people stake their lives and livelihoods on need a purpose-built system with verified, native data. That is what we build, and it is why the work is urgent. AI is reshaping how the world learns, works and earns, and the women we serve cannot afford to be left behind. We have also made a deliberate choice about how we build: a small team of exceptional people, paid well above market, each doing work that would normally take several. We would rather be ten people who move the world than thirty who move paper. That choice sets the bar for every hire, including this one. About the Role The Data Scientist, Response Evaluation, owns the math underneath UpGenie. UpGenie answers high-stakes questions about rights, law and safety, and you will decide how it scores and ranks evidence, how we measure whether an answer is right, how confident the system needs to be before it answers, and how we balance accuracy against latency and cost. The answer to a rights question can change at every level of government: federal law, the 50 states and DC, and about 90,000 local governments, which the US Census Bureau counts as counties, cities, towns, and school and special districts. Our system retrieves and ranks evidence across federal, state and local law in several domains, and our evaluation results drive real product decisions. You will make sure those decisions rest on things we can reason about: scoring functions whose behavior we understand, metrics with confidence intervals, thresholds with stated guarantees, and experiments with enough power to separate signal from noise. The role suits someone trained in mathematics, statistics or a quantitative science who has turned that training into working software. You can derive an estimator and prove its properties, then implement it, test it on real data and ship it. You will ship to production from your first weeks, with real users and real partners depending on what you build. What You’ll Own 1. Ranking and Retrieval Math The scoring functions behind search and ranking: lexical scoring, embedding similarity, hybrid score fusion, learning-to-rank, re-ranking and diversity. You will know the geometry of the embedding spaces we use and where it breaks down. 2. Evaluation Statistics Metric design, sampling plans, confidence intervals, significance and power, inter-annotator agreement, and correction for noisy automated judges. Every number we report comes with its uncertainty. 3. Calibration and Abstention Confidence scores that mean what they say. You will calibrate model scores, set abstention and escalation rules with explicit error guarantees, and decide when the system should ask a follow-up question instead of answering. 4. Optimization and Model Improvement Objectives and loss functions for fine-tuning and ranking models, principled hyperparameter and prompt search, and a clear model of the trade-off between accuracy, latency and cost, so product decisions rest on numbers. 5. Monitoring and Data Quality Catch quality changes as they happen: shifts in query and document distributions, embedding drift across model versions, change-points in production metrics, and duplicate or near-duplicate content at scale. 6. Decision Support Short, precise analyses that product, engineering and partners can act on. Lead with the answer, show the math, then say it in plain English, including what the data does not support. No false precision: 92.37% on 150 cases is not a finding. Who We’re Looking For We hire across levels. Depth of understanding and results you can show matter more than titles or years of experience. We will ask you to solve problems and build during our process, because we have learned that knowing the math and applying it to messy, real systems are different skills. Deep Mathematical Foundations Probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization at the level of derivations and proofs, not just library calls. You can tell when an assumption is doing the real work in an argument. You Ship Working Code You are fluent in Python with NumPy, SciPy and pandas, and you work in PyTorch or JAX. Your analyses are reproducible and tested, and they run in production, not only in a notebook. Statistical Judgment You know when a difference is noise. You design the experiment before you run it, and you report uncertainty by default. Rigor In our domain, a confident wrong answer can harm someone. You test before you claim, you measure before you optimize, and you flag what you are unsure about. You keep facts, inferences and assumptions separate. High Agency You unblock yourself. Given an ambiguous problem with no owner in sight, you scope it, propose an approach and build. A Clear Communicator You can explain a confidence interval to a non-technical partner and defend a modeling choice to a senior researcher, in plain words either way. Even Better If You have a graduate degree or research experience in mathematics, statistics, theoretical computer science, physics or a related field. You have worked on information retrieval, ranking, recommender systems or search quality. You have built evaluation, experimentation or A/B testing infrastructure for machine learning systems. You have used Bayesian methods, causal inference, conformal prediction or sequential testing on real problems. You have worked with Vertex AI, GCP or comparable cloud ML stacks. You have public work we can look at: papers, open source, technical writing or competition results. Before You Apply We want to be direct about what this is. This is a high-bar role on a small team, with real ownership and high expectations. Because our products work in high-stakes domains, we value rigor over shortcuts. Speed matters, but so does knowing when an elegant model or a plausible-looking result needs a closer look. If you want a pure research role, or a defined lane with clearly separated responsibilities, this is not the right fit, and that is fine. If you want to bring mathematical rigor to a system people depend on, we want to hear from you. Our interview process is thorough, and we will walk you through every step of it in our first conversation. How We Work at Uplevyl We finish what we start, and we do it well. We follow through on what we say we’ll do, and we care about the difference our work makes. We listen before we decide. Before we act, we ask who it actually affects: a customer, a partner, a teammate or the communities we serve. Trust here is built the plain way, by consistently showing up for people. We move with ownership and urgency. We don’t wait for perfect information or for someone else to raise their hand. If something looks like it could go wrong, we say so early. We make the call, we move fast, and we hold a high bar for quality. We are better together than alone. We work across teams, say what we actually think, and go out of our way to help each other succeed. Leadership here is measured by the impact you create. We stay curious and keep learning, including how to use AI well. We hold ourselves to the bar we’re building toward: questioning our own assumptions and using AI to think better and move faster.

full_description: Job Opening: Data Analytics & Business Intelligence (BI) Trainer Company: Analytix Learning Academy Location: Hyderabad, Telangana Work Mode: Classroom / Online / Hybrid (as applicable) Employment Type: Full-time / Contract (as applicable) Experience: 2–5+ years of relevant industry or hands-on project experience Open Positions: 1 About Analytix Learning Academy Analytix Learning Academy offers practical, industry-oriented training programmes in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. We are seeking a passionate and technically strong Data Analytics & BI Trainer to train students and graduates in Excel, SQL, Python for analytics, statistics, Power BI, data modelling, dashboards and AI-enabled business intelligence. The ideal candidate should combine hands-on analytics expertise with the ability to teach concepts clearly, demonstrate real business use cases and mentor students through practical projects. Job Summary The trainer will deliver the Analytics Foundation stage of our Applied Data Science & AI Engineer programme, covering business problem-solving, Excel, statistics, SQL, Python-based data analysis, AI-assisted development, Power BI, DAX, data modelling, AI in BI and introductory Generative AI and Agentic AI applications for analytics. The role involves instructor-led training, live demonstrations, practical assignments, project mentoring, assessments and technical interview preparation. Key Responsibilities1. Technical Training & Curriculum Delivery Teach Excel fundamentals, advanced formulas, lookup functions, PivotTables, Power Query and dashboard development. Explain business problem framing, KPI identification, data interpretation and analytical thinking. Deliver statistics and probability sessions covering descriptive statistics, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, correlation, regression and A/B testing. Teach SQL using MySQL or PostgreSQL, including querying, filtering, joins, aggregation, subqueries, CTEs and window functions. Train students in Python for data analysis, including fundamentals, functions, data structures, NumPy, Pandas, APIs and data cleaning. Teach exploratory data analysis (EDA), data quality validation, outlier analysis and data visualisation. Deliver Power BI training covering data connections, Power Query, ETL, star schema, relationships, DAX, calculated columns, measures and advanced DAX. Explain dashboard design, interactive reports, drill-through, tooltips, bookmarks, row-level security and data storytelling. Introduce Power BI Service, publishing, scheduled refresh, workspaces and performance optimisation. Demonstrate AI-assisted Excel, SQL and DAX development using appropriate AI tools. Introduce AI in BI, forecasting, anomaly detection, AI-assisted reporting and Generative AI concepts. Demonstrate introductory RAG and Agentic AI workflows for analytics, including automated reporting and business insight summaries. 2. Practical Training & Real-World Projects Conduct live demonstrations, hands-on labs and guided exercises using business datasets. Create industry-oriented assignments based on sales, finance, HR, marketing, banking and operations. Mentor students through module-wise mini projects, including: Excel sales performance dashboard and business recommendations. SQL analysis of banking or customer transaction data. Python-based EDA and data quality reporting. Power BI HR attrition dashboard and retention recommendations. AI-assisted sales reporting and insight automation. Guide students in converting business requirements into KPIs, analytical questions and dashboard specifications. Teach students to interpret results, identify trends and communicate actionable recommendations. Review project documentation, dashboards and presentations. 3. Student Assessment & Mentoring Prepare daily practice tasks and module-wise assignments. Conduct weekly examinations, practical assessments and timed SQL or analytics tests. Conduct technical mock interviews and assess students' understanding of concepts. Evaluate mini projects and capstone projects using structured assessment rubrics. Provide individual feedback, additional practice and remediation where required. Monitor attendance, assignment completion, assessment scores and overall student progress. Help learners develop portfolio-ready projects and prepare for Data Analyst and BI Analyst interviews. 4. Curriculum Development & Academic Coordination Prepare lesson plans, presentations, datasets, practical exercises, assignments and assessment materials. Follow the approved curriculum and maintain training schedules. Develop case studies based on realistic business problems and industry scenarios. Coordinate with other trainers to ensure a smooth transition from analytics foundations to Data Science and AI Engineering. Work with academic and placement teams to support student readiness. Incorporate relevant developments in Power BI, analytics automation and AI-assisted business intelligence. Required Technical Skills Must-have skills Advanced Excel, including formulas, PivotTables and Power Query. SQL using MySQL or PostgreSQL. Statistics and probability for business analytics. Python for data analysis, including Pandas, NumPy and data visualisation. Power BI Desktop, Power Query, data modelling and DAX. Dashboard development, KPI reporting and data storytelling. Hands-on analytical problem-solving using real or representative business datasets. Preferred additional skills Power BI Service, workspace management, scheduled refresh and row-level security. Exposure to Tableau or other BI platforms. AI-assisted analytics using ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot. Basic understanding of Generative AI, LLMs, RAG and Agentic AI workflows. Familiarity with tools such as n8n, BigQuery, dbt or Microsoft Fabric. Experience using Git/GitHub for project documentation and portfolio development. Educational Qualifications B.E./B.Tech, MCA, M.Sc., MBA Analytics or a related qualification preferred. Relevant certifications in Microsoft Power BI, analytics or related technologies are an advantage. Strong practical experience and demonstrable projects will be valued. Experience Requirements Demonstrable hands-on experience in Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, reporting or related roles. Experience with business dashboards, SQL analysis and analytical reporting. Prior experience in technical training, mentoring, corporate training or academic instruction is preferred. Candidates must be able to demonstrate their technical skills through a practical assessment. Preferred Candidate Profile Excellent communication and presentation skills. Ability to explain technical and statistical concepts to beginners. Strong analytical thinking and business problem-solving skills. Comfortable managing classroom sessions and supporting individual learners. Patient, approachable and committed to student development. Able to connect technical concepts with real business decisions. Performance Expectations Complete assigned modules within the agreed training schedule. Deliver hands-on practical sessions and industry-oriented case studies. Conduct regular assessments and provide timely feedback. Ensure students complete module-wise assignments, mini projects and capstone milestones. Support student portfolios, mock interviews and job readiness. How to Apply Interested candidates may share their updated resume, LinkedIn profile and sample dashboards or project portfolio.
